question.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=3,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=1$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ a & 0 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}c & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ a & 0 & b\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$

current_example.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are $\lambda_1={\color{blue}-1},$ $\lambda_2={\color{red}1},$ $\lambda_3=0,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/3caf3a359f6afa39a17ee832e0c87a767816524ccb037df75d32569a0f34bad2.svg)

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda_1={\color{blue}-1},$

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda_2={\color{red}1},$ and

- the $3$rd column is the eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda_3=0.$

Therefore, we get

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/d666686d07fda7036fae3554a931e984ca59a3da947245201f240c88d60f1bef.svg)

Finally, we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/9da62e7f15b2005f6246a0d2fb67e3ecfeffd6b01a6463c10631fdcdeb94b42b.svg)

In conclusion, we get $a=0,$ $b=-1,$ and $c=-1.$
